title: Range Risks
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/0/bod: Sooner or later, price **closes outside the range** with a strong candle. That's called a **breakout**. A valid breakout usually comes with **high volume**. This is exactly where reversion traders take their biggest losses.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/1/bod: Before a breakout, you often see some clues: a Bollinger **squeeze**, **repeated hits** on one edge, **higher** lows under the range top and **rising volume**. Major news can also break a range overnight.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/1/tip: Check the economic calendar before every range trade.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/2/pro: Tap the first candle that closed above the range top.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/2/exp: This candle closed above 1.0860 with a long body and high volume. That's the real breakout. The earlier candle that only wicked above the top and closed below it wasn't a breakout.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/3/sta: When price closes below the range bottom with a strong candle and high volume, buying the lower band is still a good reversion trade.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/3/exp: After a valid breakout, the market probably isn't ranging anymore, and cheap can get cheaper. Reversion rules only hold inside a range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/4/pro: The range just broke to the downside with a strong candle. What should a reversion trader do?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/4/opt: Stop taking reversion buys and wait for a new range
Double the buy size to lower the average price
Move the stop lower so it doesn't get hit
Buy with no stop, since price is even cheaper now
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/4/exp: A breakout means the conditions the strategy was built for are gone. The other options add risk exactly when the market is against you.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/5/bod: After a breakout, price often comes back and tests the **broken edge** from the other side: **old support** now acts as **resistance**. You're no longer looking for reversion buys here. The market has probably started trending.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/6/pro: Gold broke the range bottom (2380), came back up under it, and got rejected with an upper wick. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/6/exp: The broken support is now resistance, and the upper wick shows sellers are active there. More downside is likely. If price closes back above 2380, this scenario is invalid.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/7/sen: After the range bottom breaks, old support may act as ___, and the better-suited strategy is ___.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l1/steps/7/exp: A broken level flips its role, and a market that's broken out of its range responds better to trend methods.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/0/bod: That's the most dangerous sentence in mean reversion. If the range breaks, a trade with no stop loss can turn a small loss into a **big loss**. **Averaging down** (buying more while you're losing) without a stop only makes things worse.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/0/tip: A strategy that's usually right gets wiped out by one big mistake if it has no stop loss.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/1/bod: The most sensible spot is just **beyond the edge of the range**, with a **buffer** (a few pips or part of the ATR) so normal wicks don't hit it. If price gets there, the range has probably broken and your idea is invalid.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/2/pro: You sell near the range top at 1.2731. Which line is the more sensible stop loss?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/2/exp: A sits just above the range highs (around 1.2742) with a buffer. B is below the highs and gets hit by a normal wick. C is so far away that its risk is much bigger than the profit to mid-range.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/3/pro: Your account is $5,000 and you risk 1%. Your stop is 25 pips, and one pip on 1 standard lot of EUR/USD is worth $10. How many lots do you trade?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/3/exp: 50 ÷ 25 = $2 per pip. Each lot is $10 per pip, so 2 ÷ 10 = 0.2 lots. If your stop gets hit, you lose exactly $50.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/4/sta: If price gets close to your stop loss, pushing the stop back helps give your idea a chance.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/4/exp: Pushing your stop back means you raised your risk mid-trade. Your stop is where your idea is proven wrong, so never move it toward a bigger loss.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/5/bod: In a range, price usually heads back toward the mean fairly quickly. If it still hasn't after a few candles (say 10), many traders close the trade. That's called a **time stop**. The range might be turning into a trend.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/6/pro: You took a reversion entry and 12 candles have passed. Price hasn't hit your stop or moved toward the mean. Your time stop rule is 10 candles. What do you do?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/6/opt: Follow the rule and close the trade
Add to the position to reach profit faster
Remove the stop to give it room
Wait as long as it takes
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/6/exp: A reversion that's taking too long is a sign the idea is weak. You wrote the rule in advance so you wouldn't make decisions on hope mid-trade.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/7/pro: Put the steps for setting the stop and size on a range-bottom buy in order.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/7/ite: Add a buffer below the bottom
Measure the distance from entry to stop
Work out the size from your risk amount
Place the order with the stop loss
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/7/exp: First you find the logical stop on the chart, then you size the trade so a possible loss equals your risk amount.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/8/sen: Buying more while a trade is losing is called ___, and in mean reversion it's very dangerous without a ___.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l2/steps/8/exp: Pyramiding means adding to a winning trade. Averaging down is the opposite, and with no cap on losses it multiplies a single mistake.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/0/bod: A **trend filter** is a simple rule that tells you when, and in which direction, you're allowed to take reversion trades. For example: if price is **above the SMA 200** on the higher timeframe, only **buying pullbacks** is allowed, and selling the upper band is off-limits.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/0/tip: With a trend filter, mean reversion turns into buying the dip within a trend.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/1/bod: One simple filter is the **slope of the average**. Many traders also use **ADX**: it measures trend strength, and a reading below about **20** usually means the trend is weak.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/1/exa: Buy and sell at the edges
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/2/pro: Using the average-slope filter (SMA 20, the gold line), which reversion trade is allowed?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/2/opt: Only sells when price stretches up
Only buys when price stretches down
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/2/exp: The average points down, and price is making lower highs and lower lows. The filter only allows selling after price comes back up toward the average. Buying the lows is going against the current.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/3/sta: Many traders see an ADX below about 20 as a sign of a weak trend or a trendless market.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/3/exp: ADX measures trend strength regardless of direction. A low reading means the trend is weak, and conditions suit mean reversion better.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/4/pro: Ethereum is in an uptrend and the SMA 20 is rising. Price pulled back near the average, RSI dropped from above 70 to about 40, and the last candle is a hammer. What's the more likely next move?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/4/exp: This is mean reversion in the direction of the trend: the filter only allows buys, and a pullback to the average with a hammer is a good chance. But if price closes below the hammer's low, the idea is invalid.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/5/pro: On the daily chart, price is below a falling SMA 200. On the 1-hour, price has reached the upper Bollinger Band and RSI is at 75. With a trend filter, what do you do?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/5/exp: The big trend is down, so only selling the rallies is allowed. Reaching the upper band with high RSI is exactly where the filter lets you sell.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/6/pai: Trend direction on the current chart
The big picture before you enter
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/7/pro: Put the checklist for a trend-filtered reversion trade in order.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/7/ite: Wait for price to stretch from the mean
Spot a reversal sign in the allowed direction
Enter with a stop and the mean as target
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/7/exp: The filter comes first: before hunting for signals, figure out which direction you're even allowed to trade.
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/8/pro: Put it all together. What's the best decision?
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/8/opt: Wait until after the news; if the setup still holds, buy
Buy right now with double size
Buy with no stop before the news
lessons/mean-reversion-u3-l3/steps/8/exp: The setup fits the trend filter, but major news can break any level in an instant. Waiting until after the news cuts the risk of a nasty surprise.
